title: 1.78mJ/Frame 373fps 3D GS Processor Based on Shape-Aware Hybrid Architecture Using Earlier Computation Skipping and Gaussian Cache Scheduler
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3D GS) rendering on edge devices suffers from variable Gaussian distribution shapes requiring complex projection+rasterization dataflow, diverse input-dependent inefficient computations, and irregular memory access patterns for millions of spherical-harmonic coefficients.
motivation: 3D GS offers superior speed and accuracy over Neural Radiance Fields for VR and embodied AI, but edge device deployment (e.g., Xavier NX achieving only 6.4fps) is severely limited by power consumption and memory footprint.
method: The processor employs a shape-aware hybrid architecture that detects and skips redundant computations based on Gaussian properties, uses early computation termination when results become insignificant, and implements a smart Gaussian cache scheduler to reduce irregular off-chip memory traffic for SH coefficients.
key_novelty: Shape-aware early computation skipping and intelligent Gaussian cache scheduling to mitigate input-dependent inefficiencies and memory bottlenecks in 3D GS rendering.
contributions: Identifies and exploits input-dependent computation redundancy in variable Gaussian distributions
Proposes earlier computation skipping mechanism with adaptive early termination
Introduces Gaussian cache scheduler to optimize spherical-harmonic coefficient access patterns
Achieves 373fps at 1.78mJ/frame on edge device vs. 6.4fps on Xavier NX baseline
limitations: Evaluation focused on edge deployment; comparison with GPU/high-end implementations not discussed.
primary_theme: Shape-aware edge 3D Gaussian Splatting processor with computation skipping
